metadata.note: The Black Mountain Railway (organized April 21, 1910, North Carolina): a Yancey County lumber road from Kona on the Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio up the Toe valleys to Burnsville, then up the Cane River to Pensacola, Murchison and Eskota under Mount Mitchell. Revenue passengers 1914-1927 (company returns to the NC Corporation Commission). One company and one colour throughout: Holston Corporation / Clinchfield control from 1913 was financial and the Black Mountain ran its own trains, so there is no Rule 4 split. Not to be confused with the Black Mountain Railway of Virginia (bought by the Virginia and Southwestern in 1908) or the Mount Mitchell Railroad from the town of Black Mountain, NC.

Passenger train vs mixed train, and the real frequency: every headway on this layer is an estimate.

Track-removal date west of Burnsville: 1926 (Wikipedia), 1926-28 (clinchfield.org), 1928 (Trains 1974), 1933 (1981 Yancey County survey) - recorded, not resolved.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line legs. Drawn on OSM way 18941655 (railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=Clinchfield, note:old_railway_operator=Black Mountain), which the OSM mapper flags 'rough alignment in places ... physical evidence of the railway [is] long gone' - so this is a reconstructed grade of uneven precision, not surveyed track. Its first 29 nodes (the curve off the Clinchfield main line at Kona, starting 7 m from CSX Blue Ridge Subdivision way 238231339) were spliced in from the way itself because waypoint snapping skipped them. Traced 11.5 mi against 10.6 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide; Fowler) - about 8% long, consistent with the 'rough alignment' fixme; Kona - Pensacola as traced totals 19.9 mi against Fowler's 20.4, so some of the excess is where the Burnsville split is placed. The Burnsville end is pinned where this way meets the NC 197-tagged grade (35.9052N, 82.2942W), ~1.4 km SE of the town-boundary centroid Nominatim returns; the depot's exact position is not sourced. One leg is effectively straight: the way's own last two nodes span 0.53 mi (860 m) as a ruled line from 35.9116N, 82.2889W down to the Burnsville pin. That is the OSM mapper's rough reconstruction, not a surveyed curve, and it is the least reliable piece of this trace. Waypoint fit: Kona 0.0 km, Bacchus 0.0, Micaville 0.1, Windom 0.0. The Micaville - Bowditch spur is freight-only and NOT drawn. Era: the line was never relocated in the passenger era as far as is known; the OSM way is a reconstruction of the original grade, not a later alignment.

segments.note: Kona (junction with the Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio at Clinchfield MP 173.5) - Backus/Bacchus - Micaville - Windom - Burnsville, 10.6 mi up the North Toe and South Toe valleys. The line opened Kona - Micaville - Bowditch on July 8, 1911 (ICC valuation) as a freight and lumber carrier: the company's FY1913 return to the NC Corporation Commission reports no passenger revenue. Revenue passengers first appear in the return for July 1913 - June 1914 (3,702), so 1914 is drawn as the start; whether passengers rode in late 1913 is not established. Ridership peaked near 44,000 in 1919-1920 and fell with the timber (11,408 in 1924; 1,013 in calendar 1927). Sunday passenger service was discontinued by Commission order of Dec 5, 1924. No passenger count is printed for 1928 or any later year, and by 1930 the small 'passenger train' revenue line is labelled '(express)' - so 1927 is the last passenger year; the exact date in 1927/early 1928 is not established. Context only, not drawn (Rule 1): the road ran freight and express only from 1928 (Feb 1952 Official Guide: 'Operated for freight and express service only'), was sold in 1954-55 and ran as the Yancey Railroad from April 1, 1955 until late 1982. The Black Mountain ran its own trains throughout; Holston Corporation / Clinchfield control from 1913 was financial, so there is no ownership split. headway_min 1440 (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE from the Kona, NC Wikipedia article's unsourced 'daily roundtrip passenger and mixed train service' and the 1916 crew count (2 enginemen, 2 conductors); no timetable was read, and passenger-vs-mixed train is unresolved.
sources: Segment-level: the 1914 start (first revenue passengers, FY to June 30, 1914; none in FY1913), the 1927 end (last year with revenue passengers; none reported 1928-1933, express only by 1930) and the Dec 5, 1924 Sunday-service order are read from the company's own returns printed in the NC Corporation Commission reports below; clinchfield.org independently gives 1914-1927. The headway is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line legs. Drawn on OSM ways 1323989933, 1323989934, 679611336 and 679611335 - NC 197 road centreline, tagged railway=abandoned + old_railway_operator=Clinchfield + note:old_railway_operator=Black Mountain (the highway was built on the grade). Traced 8.4 mi against ~9.8 mi documented (Fowler: Burnsville 10.6, Pensacola 20.4) - about 14% short. Part of that is the Burnsville split point (see the Kona - Burnsville feature, which runs ~0.9 mi long), and part is that the line ends at the Pensacola junction on the main line (the Cane River bridge, where Nominatim also places Pensacola): the 0.337-mi Pensacola BRANCH shown in the ICC valuation is not in OSM and is NOT drawn. LATER ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): this draws the modern NC 197 road, which OSM says occupies the grade; highway construction may have eased curves, so it is the road's line, not verified 1913 track. Waypoints were placed on the grade (Burnsville junction; the 35.8750N, 82.3201W bend; Pensacola); Nominatim's Low Gap point lies 1.9 km east of the grade (the community, not the station) and was not used.

segments.note: Burnsville - Dellingers - Low Gap - Pensacola (Fowler mileposts 10.6 to 20.4), up the Cane River on the grade later used by NC 197; Bowditch - Pensacola opened Aug 10, 1913 (ICC valuation). The company's FY1914 and FY1915 returns describe the road operated as 'Kona, N.C., to Pensacola, N.C.', and the 1915 company public timetable on Fowler's station list includes Pensacola, so passengers are drawn from 1914 (same FY bracket as Kona - Burnsville). A 1916 complaint by 'Citizens of Pensacola and Eskota' asked for ADDITIONAL passenger trains. The NC Corporation Commission's order of Dec 5, 1924 discontinued Sunday passenger service 'between Kona ... and Pensacola' and made Pensacola a non-agency station, which shows weekday trains still running to Pensacola in Dec 1924. 1924 is the LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END [OPEN]: the system carried passengers to 1927 and the road operated still reached west of Burnsville in 1925-27, but no source says whether trains ran past Burnsville after 1924. Do not extend without evidence. Track west of Burnsville was authorised for removal under ICC Finance Docket 5537 (NC hearing Sept 27, 1926); removal dates in secondary sources range 1926-1933 - abandonment is not the passenger end. Pensacola itself sat on a 0.337-mi branch off the main line to Murchison and Eskota (not drawn). headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (see Kona - Burnsville).
sources: Segment-level: the 1914 start (FY1914/FY1915 returns, road operated 'Kona to Pensacola'), the 1916 complaint and the Dec 5, 1924 order (p.76) - the last segment-specific confirmed year - are from the NC Corporation Commission reports below; Fowler's 1915 timetable list names Pensacola. The [OPEN] end and the headway are NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line legs. Drawn from the Pensacola junction on the main line over OSM way 18942204 (NC 197, railway=abandoned + old_railway_operator=Clinchfield + note:old_railway_operator=Black Mountain) to Murchison, way 18941261 (Ewart Wilson Road / SR 1100, same tags) and way 169481126 (Ewart Wilson Road, railway=abandoned with no operator tag, 0.7 mi), which ends exactly at Nominatim's Eskota hamlet point. Traced 3.8 mi against Fowler's 3.6 (Pensacola 20.4 - Murchison 21.5 - Eskota 24) and the ICC valuation's 2.980 mi Pensacola - Eskota (measured from the Pensacola branch end; mileage conflict recorded in metadata). Pensacola - Murchison traces 1.2 mi vs Fowler 1.1; Murchison - Eskota 2.5 mi vs Fowler 2.5. Waypoint fit: Pensacola 0.1 km, Murchison 0.0, Eskota 0.0. LATER ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): this draws the modern road centrelines OSM places on the grade, not verified 1913 track.

segments.note: Pensacola junction - Murchison - Eskota, the terminal 'under the shadow of Mount Mitchell' (NC Corporation Commission, 1926). Pensacola - Eskota was built from April 1913 and opened Oct 13, 1913 (ICC valuation). Eskota and Murchison both appear on Fowler's station list taken from the 1915 company public timetable, so 1915 is the first drawn year; whether the FY1914 passengers reached Eskota is unknown, so 1914 is not claimed. The 1916 complaint of 'Citizens of Pensacola and Eskota' asked for ADDITIONAL passenger trains, i.e. trains already ran. 1916 is the LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END [OPEN]: nothing found confirms passenger trains past Pensacola after 1916, and the Dec 1924 order's wording ('between Kona ... and Pensacola') suggests, but does not prove, that they no longer reached Eskota by then. Do not extend without evidence. Track Burnsville - Eskota was authorised for removal from late 1926. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (an unsourced Wikipedia line describes a daily train to Murchison).
sources: Segment-level: 1915 from Fowler's list of stations on the 1915 company public timetable (Murchison 21.5, Eskota 24); 1916 from the NC Corporation Commission's 1916 report (Pensacola and Eskota passenger-service complaint). The [OPEN] end and the headway are NOT sourced.
